narrative:
I set out to kill OPP-07 and I got closer than the spec's own 61 suggests, but not all the way. The demand half is genuinely the best-evidenced thing in this portfolio and I could not dent it. The product half, the price and above all the FIXTURE argument are where it breaks.

The spec stakes everything on one sentence: 'Nike already sells women's basketball shorts; what it does not sell is a short standing next to the jersey it matches.' It then makes that literal - 'If the fixture change cannot be secured with Dick's/Foot Locker, the product should not be made, because the fixture IS the opportunity.' That sentence is checkable on the open web, and it does not hold. Fanatics operates a dedicated Ladies WNBA Shorts navigation category, sitting inside the same fan storefront as the jerseys, and the product in it is largely Nike: Women's Legends Flow Mesh Shorts at USD 74.99, Legends Relaxed Fit Fleece Shorts at USD 74.99, Women's 2026 On-Court Dri-FIT Victory team shorts at USD 84.99, Logowoman Team 13 Crossover at USD 49.99, Team 13 Tri-Blend 8 inch biker at USD 79.99. The WNBA Store carries a Women's WNBA Nike Studio Fleece Short. Nike's own WNBA fan assortment shows Victory knee-length at USD 85, Basketball Fleece at USD 75 and a Women's Crossover WNBA short at USD 60. And Nike shipped the Rebel Fanwear short - jersey, hoodie, tee, short, team-designed - on 8 May 2026 into nike.com, lockervision, team stores and select retailers. All of these are fan-coded, fan-priced, fan-merchandised women's basketball bottoms hanging with the jerseys today. The unserved condition the opportunity is named after is already served, by Nike, in the exact doors the spec asks for. This is also, precisely, why the cross-dataset auditor REJECTED A05-O4 'Game-Day Women's Fan-to-Court Short' four weeks ago. OPP-07 is written to dodge that rejection by relocating the novelty from 'team-identity fan short' to 'fixture plus proportion', but only half of that dodge survives: the fixture half is falsified, and only the proportion half is left.

The price collapses on the same evidence. The spec's entire USD 65-75 argument is that moving to the fan fixture swaps a USD 37-65 performance comparison set for a USD 80-85 fan comparison set. But the USD 80-85 fan wall is a LIST wall. The same Fanatics assortment shows those tickets clearing with codes - the Logowoman Crossover at USD 34.97 from USD 49.99, the Tri-Blend biker at USD 55.99 from USD 79.99, On-Court Victory at USD 45.49-64.99 from USD 84.99. That is 25-45% off, which is the same or worse than the USD 42.97-from-USD-65 Sabrina markdown the spec correctly called its most important price fact. The fan fixture is not a higher-realised-price environment; it is a higher-list, equally-promotional one. Against A03-S9 (FY26 apparel units +1%, ASP contributing about 1 point, already partly offset by discounts and channel mix) and A04-S4, a USD 65 core rung with a USD 75 drop is not a hypothesis to test, it is a number to abandon. Cost it at USD 50-55 or do not cost it.

The newness problem compounds. The Caitlin Clark Nike apparel collection - tees, HOODIES, SWEATPANTS and BASKETBALL SHORTS with the double-C logo on the leg, adult and grade-school sizes, Nike.com plus partner retailers, with the full signature apparel line following - is exactly a fan-coded women's-basketball bottom sold as part of an outfit, already in market. Nike now runs three women's basketball signature apparel programmes (Sabrina, A'One, Clark) plus WNBA Victory, Rebel Fanwear, Legends Flow Mesh and Legends Fleece. The auditor's instruction on the surviving residual of A01-O2 was explicit: a true women's-graded block with waist/hip/rise engineering 'should be routed as an input to the existing Clark/A'One apparel program, not as a standalone new opportunity.' My attack ends in the same place. The one thing in OPP-07 that is genuinely unserved and genuinely valuable - a women's high-rise, untapered block that reads as an outfit rather than as kit - is a BLOCK DECISION, and block decisions belong inside programmes Nike is already funding.

What survived my attack, and survived it cleanly: the demand. Three consecutive record WNBA seasons on a per-game basis, an All-Star crowd that outdrew the NBA's, 73 million unique viewers at the halfway point, a seven-year CBA with the cap up roughly fivefold, all of it achieved with Caitlin Clark sidelined for much of 2026 - the audit's hype-vs-sustained verdict is 'sustained' and it is one of the only places in this base where new evidence made a signal stronger. A05-S7's Unrivaled economics are VERIFIED. A04-S5's Ed Stack call-out is a first-party retailer demand statement. A02-S7's wholesale swing is VERIFIED. Nike's right to win is structural and real: only Nike controls the trim, placket, colour standard and drop calendar on both halves, because only Nike holds the on-court licence. None of that is in question.

So the honest verdict is a split one. Women's basketball is the right place to spend. 'The Other Half' is not the right reason. The opportunity does not survive as written - its stated kill condition has already been met and it does not know it - but the underlying bet survives in reduced form, at a materially lower confidence, and the decisive tests are cheaper and closer to hand than the spec thinks: Nike already owns the Rebel Fanwear and Clark shorts sell-through numbers, which are a far better instrument than one night of Unrivaled receipts at a two-season startup league Nike has no contractual right to.

One methodological caveat I have to state, because the spec was scrupulous about it and I must be too: every retail domain I tried this session was blocked by the egress proxy - nike.com, fanatics.com, wnbastore.nba.com, dickssportinggoods.com, about.nike.com, frontofficesports.com, klarna.com. Every price and assortment fact above is a search-engine summary, not a retrieved product page, exactly the standard of evidence the audit warned about. That cuts both ways: it means my kill shots need confirmation, and it means the spec's price section rests on the same sand. The difference is that my finding can be confirmed by one buyer walking one Dick's fan wall in an afternoon.

kill_attempts.angle: Is it NEW? The fixture premise - 'Nike does not sell a short standing next to the jersey it matches'
kill_attempts.argument: The load-bearing claim of the whole opportunity, and the one it says should decide whether the product gets made, is that Nike's women's basketball bottoms sit on the performance grid and are absent from the fan fixture. If a Nike women's basketball short is already merchandised in the fan door alongside the jersey, at a fan price, in a fan aesthetic, then the 'occasion retarget and fixture change' is not a change - it is a description of the current state, and there is no opportunity left except a pattern revision.
kill_attempts.evidence: Fanatics runs a dedicated Ladies WNBA Shorts category (https://www.fanatics.com/wnba/women-shorts/o-2537+ga-80+d-64990107+z-9514-3743804646) inside the same storefront as WNBA jerseys, stocked substantially with Nike women's fan product: Legends Flow Mesh Shorts USD 74.99, Legends Relaxed Fit Fleece Shorts USD 74.99, Women's 2026 On-Court Dri-FIT Victory team shorts USD 84.99, Logowoman Team 13 Crossover USD 49.99, Team 13 Tri-Blend 8in Biker USD 79.99. WNBAStore lists a Women's WNBA Nike Studio Fleece Short (https://wnbastore.nba.com/women/ga-35+z-6540047-775122636). Nike's own WNBA fan pages show Victory knee-length USD 85, Basketball Fleece USD 75, Women's Crossover WNBA USD 60 (https://www.nike.com/w/wnba-shorts-38fphz6ef6n). And Nike shipped the Rebel Fanwear collection - hoodie, tee and SHORT, team-designed - on 8 May 2026 to nike.com, lockervision.wnba.com, team stores and select retailers (https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-empowers-teams-to-express-their-identity-with-the-2026-wnba-rebel-edition-uniforms). All retrieved 2026-09-03 as search-result summaries; every retail domain was egress-blocked this session. This is the identical ground on which the auditor rejected A05-O4.

kill_attempts.angle: Does the consumer need exist as stated? The jersey-outfit-implies-a-bottom inference
kill_attempts.argument: The 'unserved job' rests on inferring demand for a BOTTOM from search growth on a TOP. The spec concedes this is an inference and not an observation, then builds a block, two fabrics, two inseams, a size run and a drop calendar on it. The cross-dataset auditor did not merely flag it - it instructed that the basketball-specific inference be DISCARDED.
kill_attempts.evidence: Audit contradiction 'Sport-as-fashion is real, but the data behind it is not basketball's': the same Pinterest Summer 2026 report shows 'Formula 1 aesthetic outfit' +483%, 'Brazil jersey outfit women' +302%, 'baddie tracksuit outfit' +276%, growth rates on undisclosed bases, on a female-skewing search-and-save pinboard, not purchase (A05-S4, A05-S1). Auditor verdict: 'Preserve the general finding... and discard the basketball-specific inference.' The Klarna / Sports Innovation Lab 'Rep Her' report the spec leans on measures MERCHANDISE availability generally - 60%+ of intending buyers did not purchase because product was out of stock, 79% cite gaps in variety (52%), availability (47%) and quality (36%) - and its trade coverage headline is about SHIRTS, not bottoms (https://www.klarna.com/us/shopping/blog/klarna-sports-innovation-lab/; https://uk.fashionnetwork.com/news/Women-s-sports-shirt-sales-rise-fast-but-availability-a-problem-says-klarna,1648927.html, retrieved 2026-09-03 as search summaries). Nothing in the base measures bottoms as a share of women's fan merchandise, in any geography.

kill_attempts.angle: Price: does USD 65-75 hold in the fan fixture?
kill_attempts.argument: The price is argued entirely from the comparison set - move to a fan wall neighbouring USD 80-85 product and USD 65-75 becomes defensible. That argument only works if the fan wall realises its list prices. If the fan wall discounts as hard as the performance wall, then the comparison set changes the ticket and not the take, and Nike would be adding a fourth USD 65 women's short into a fixture already clearing three of them at a third off.
kill_attempts.evidence: The same Fanatics women's WNBA shorts assortment shows the fan rung clearing with codes: Logowoman Team 13 Crossover at USD 34.97 from USD 49.99; Team 13 Tri-Blend biker at USD 55.99 from USD 79.99; On-Court Victory Performance shorts at USD 45.49-64.99 from USD 84.99 (search summary, 2026-09-03). That is 25-45% off, matching or exceeding the USD 42.97-from-USD-65 Sabrina markdown the spec itself calls its most important price fact. Against A03-S9 (VERIFIED: FY2026 apparel USD 13.4B, +2% cn, units +1%, ASP about 1 point, partly offset by higher discounts and channel mix) and A04-S4 (increasingly promotional US marketplace; Sabrina tees at USD 15.97-28.97), and with the audit's standing instruction that no price in this portfolio is anchored, the USD 65-75 rung is not a testable hypothesis - it is a number with contrary evidence on both walls.

kill_attempts.angle: Cannibalisation and in-flight duplication inside Nike
kill_attempts.argument: In a flat-unit apparel environment, a new women's fan short does not create demand; it splits it. And Nike is already building the thing at three separate signature programmes, so a standalone franchise competes for the same fan-door slot, the same buyer and the same marketing calendar as work already funded.
kill_attempts.evidence: The Caitlin Clark Nike apparel collection comprises tees, basketball SHORTS, hoodies and sweatpants with the double-C mark on the chest of tops and the leg of bottoms, in Fever navy/yellow plus black/white and white/blue, in adult and grade-school sizes, at Nike.com and partner retailers from 1 October, with signature-line apparel following (https://sneakernews.com/2025/09/25/caitlin-clark-nike-apparel-holiday-2025/, search summary retrieved 2026-09-03 - note this dates the first apparel drop to Oct 2025, where the spec dates it 1 Oct 2026). Add Sabrina and Sabrina 4 Aero-FIT (A03-S6, A03-S4), A'One, WNBA Victory, Rebel Fanwear, Legends Flow Mesh and Legends Fleece. The auditor's disposition of the identical residual idea in A01-O2 was to route a true women's-graded block 'as an input to the existing Clark/A'One apparel program, not as a standalone new opportunity.'

kill_attempts.angle: Nike's right to win with this specific consumer
kill_attempts.argument: Nike is proposing to win a fan-fashion occasion with the one consumer cohort where its own measured standing is falling, in a category (apparel, not footwear) where its teen mindshare is 26% rather than the widely-quoted 49% footwear figure - and it has not consulted the most recent survey.
kill_attempts.evidence: A01-S1: Piper Sandler spring 2025, 6,455 teens, 13-point drop among females, female share under 40% for the first time since 2020; fall-2025 coverage attributes the 'stabilisation' to the MALE upper-income bracket while stating share among girls was still declining; the spring 2026 wave exists and appears nowhere in the base. Against this, the licence position is real and exclusive: Nike supplies the WNBA on-court uniform including the 2026 Rebel Edition, holds three women's basketball signature lines, and put Aero-FIT on a women's-athlete-led signature short and jersey first (A03-S4). Mitchell & Ness has the retro fan bottom but no current on-court top; Fanatics distributes but does not design the block; adidas and Puma hold no WNBA on-court licence.

kill_attempts.angle: Timing - is SS28 the right window, or is the window closing before the product lands?
kill_attempts.argument: The whole case is a 'supply desert' first-mover window. Deserts get irrigated. Between now and SS28 delivery, Fanatics, Nike's own three signature programmes, the two 2026 expansion clubs and a wave of women's-sports DTC labels are actively filling this space. A programme that ships 18-24 months after the gap was identified arrives as a fast-follower into its own category.
kill_attempts.evidence: The supply-gap narrative is already over two years old - the '1 piece of women's merchandise for every 9 men's' framing dates to July 2024 trade coverage (https://members.asicentral.com/news/strategy/july-2024/the-supply-demand-gap-in-women-s-sports-merch-presents-opportunities/, search summary 2026-09-03) - and the assortment evidence above shows the fan-bottoms slot filling in real time between May 2026 and today. Separately, the spec's LA28 argument is asserted, not evidenced: LA28 basketball is a USOPC/federation licence question, not a WNBA one, and the audit notes LA28 appears in none of the seven source files, so it is an inference added by the developer rather than a signal.

kill_attempts.angle: Execution feasibility - fabric, cost, SKU count and manufacturing
kill_attempts.argument: The construction spec is more complex and more SKU-heavy than the demand evidence can carry, and one of its stated points of difference cannot be verified even directionally.
kill_attempts.evidence: The spec concedes nobody has established the GSM of any current Nike basketball short, so the '200-230 g/m2 heavier hand' point of difference may describe what already ships - it is a target with no baseline. Layer on: two inseams x two fabric faces (open mesh and matte tricot with a bound satin hem) x XS-3X plus tall x a four-colour core x jersey-matched Rebel and All-Star drops x one event-exclusive colourway PER Unrivaled tour stop. Bonded waistband facing, bonded and bartacked pocket bags on both sides, and a flat back-yoke zip pocket are three separate bonding/reinforcement operations on a garment priced to survive at USD 55. Event-exclusive colourways at a two-season startup league's arena volumes are a minimum-order-quantity problem, not a merchandising win. This also cuts directly against A02-S7's own VERIFIED conclusion, which the spec cites approvingly: build shorts line plans for wholesale sell-through with a replenishable core rather than drops. An extended size run offered from day one on an unforecast programme is the classic source of broken size curves and markdown.

kill_attempts.angle: The test instrument and the geographic generalisation
kill_attempts.argument: The opportunity's claim to a Council slot is the cheapness of its decisive test. But the named test may be unrunnable, is n=1, and the far better instrument is one Nike already owns and did not pull. And the whole thesis is a single-country read written into a global SS28 line.
kill_attempts.evidence: The proposed test is splitting Unrivaled's Philadelphia USD 400,000 merchandise night (A05-S7, VERIFIED) by category. Unrivaled is a privately held two-season league; Nike has no stated contractual right to its category-level receipts, and one night in one city at a novelty tour stop in an NBA arena is a sample of one whose generalisation to the WNBA the spec itself lists as unknown. Meanwhile Nike owns the Rebel Fanwear short sell-through (shipped 8 May 2026) and the Caitlin Clark shorts sell-through, and neither appears in any of the seven files. On geography: the audit puts roughly 48% of surviving signals as US-primary and closer to 70% once US-derived 'Global' signals are attributed; Europe is the primary market of zero signals; Latin America zero. A02-S9 (Australia) is the only registry-grade non-US evidence and is about PARTICIPATION, not fan merchandise. The spec excludes Greater China outright (A02-S2, A04-S2) and concedes it does not serve Worldball at all - so a global line receives a US-only seasonal fan programme.

kill_attempts.angle: Is the women's block even the right construction decision?
kill_attempts.argument: The single strongest first-party commercial signal in the whole stack describes a CROSS-GENDER buyer. If the volume buyer is male as well as female, then a women's-graded block is the wrong pattern decision derived from the right demand signal, and the correct product is a unisex fan block offered in a women's size run - which Nike already ships (Legends Relaxed Fit Fleece, Logowoman Team 13 reversible, both listed unisex).
kill_attempts.evidence: A04-S5: Ed Stack on the Dick's Q1 2026 call, first full quarter owning Foot Locker - the basketball business is coming back built around women's basketball, naming Sabrina and A'ja Wilson, with 'boys and girls, young men and women are buying that product.' The spec places this in what_we_still_dont_know while simultaneously building the entire product on a women's-specific block. Corroborating the unisex reading: Fanatics lists WNBA Nike UNISEX Logowoman Team 13 Performance Reversible Shorts and WNBA Nike UNISEX Legends Relaxed Fit Fleece Shorts at USD 74.99 in the WNBA fan assortment (search summary, 2026-09-03).

kill_attempts.angle: The coverage-first justification for the 9 inch inseam
kill_attempts.argument: The 9 inch length is justified by a signal that is classified HYPOTHESIS and sourced from one athlete quote plus two modest-dress stories, while the adjacent inseam signals in the same base were REJECTED outright for exactly this kind of sourcing. The length decision therefore has no consumer-preference evidence behind it in either direction.
kill_attempts.evidence: A05-S8 is [HYPOTHESIS | PLAUSIBLE - NEEDS VALIDATION], resting on a Brittney Griner quote, a Minnesota community team's self-designed uniforms and the French hijab-ban campaign - an inclusion argument, not a demand measurement. A01-S8 ('girls offered short inseams by default; parents push back') was REJECTED as a 2013 Today.com article with an anonymous retailer. A01-S4 was REJECTED as an SEO content farm. A05-O1's '6-inch standard' premise was REJECTED as an undated Under Armour marketing blog. A07-S6's own note that custom uniform charts default women to 6 inch is, as the spec concedes, a manufacturing convention rather than a preference. So the 7/9 ladder is a designer's judgement presented alongside evidence citations that do not support a length at all.

additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: A dedicated women's WNBA shorts fixture already exists at the largest fan retailer, inside the same storefront as the jerseys, and it is stocked substantially with Nike fan-coded product: Women's Legends Flow Mesh Shorts USD 74.99, Legends Relaxed Fit Fleece Shorts USD 74.99, Women's 2026 On-Court Dri-FIT Victory team shorts USD 84.99, Logowoman Team 13 Crossover USD 49.99, Team 13 Tri-Blend 8in Biker USD 79.99. This falsifies the opportunity's stated point of difference ('what Nike does not sell is a short standing next to the jersey it matches') and it is the same ground on which the auditor rejected A05-O4.

additional_contradictory_evidence.source: Fanatics WNBA women's shorts pricing observed with promotional codes (search-result summary; page not retrieved)
additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: The fan wall the spec uses as its USD 80-85 price anchor is discounting 25-45%: Logowoman Team 13 Crossover at USD 34.97 from USD 49.99; Team 13 Tri-Blend biker at USD 55.99 from USD 79.99; On-Court Victory at USD 45.49-64.99 from USD 84.99. The fan fixture therefore does NOT change the realised-price environment relative to the USD 42.97-from-USD-65 Sabrina rung; it changes only the list ticket. The USD 65 core / USD 75 drop argument loses its only support.

additional_contradictory_evidence.source: NIKE, Inc. Newsroom - 2026 WNBA Rebel Edition Uniforms and Rebel Fanwear (search-result summary; about.nike.com egress-blocked)
additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: The Rebel Fanwear retail collection - hoodie, T-shirt and SHORT, taking design cues from the Rebel Edition uniform colours and graphics, co-designed with all 15 teams - has been available since 8 May 2026 at nike.com, lockervision.wnba.com, team stores and select retailers. A Nike jersey-matched women's-market fan short in fan doors is a shipping product, not an opportunity. Its sell-through is the decisive test and it appears in none of the seven source files.

additional_contradictory_evidence.source: SneakerNews - Caitlin Clark's first Nike apparel collection (search-result summary; domain egress-blocked)
additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: The Clark collection is t-shirts, basketball shorts, hoodies and sweatpants with the double-C logo on the chest of tops and the leg of bottoms, in Fever colours plus black/white and white/blue, adult and grade-school, at Nike.com and partner retailers from 1 October, with the signature shoe and apparel line following in 2026. This is a fan-coded women's-basketball outfit including a bottom, already at retail - and it dates the first apparel drop a year earlier than the spec's '1 October 2026'. Directly relevant to the cannibalisation and duplication tests, and to A01-O2's rejection reason.

additional_contradictory_evidence.source: Klarna / Sports Innovation Lab 'Rep Her' report and trade coverage (search-result summaries; klarna.com and fashionnetwork egress-blocked)
additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: The report the spec uses as its 'supply desert' proof measures merchandise availability in general - over 60% of intending buyers did not purchase because product was out of stock; 79% cite a men's/women's gap in variety (52%), availability (47%) and quality (36%); 32% cannot find a retailer carrying their team or athlete. It quantifies a DISTRIBUTION and STOCK problem, not a garment-type gap, and its trade coverage is headlined on shirts. It contains no bottoms-versus-tops evidence, so it cannot support the claim that the missing item is a short. If anything, 'not in stock' argues for deeper buys of what already exists.

additional_contradictory_evidence.source: Nike WNBA shorts assortment (search-result summary; nike.com egress-blocked)
additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: Nike's own WNBA fan shorts assortment shows a Women's Dri-FIT Victory knee-length short at USD 85 in team versions, Basketball Fleece shorts at USD 75, and a Women's Nike Crossover WNBA short at USD 60 - i.e. Nike already occupies USD 60-85 in women's WNBA fan bottoms across mesh, fleece and knee-length. The proposed USD 65 core lands in the middle of a rung Nike already owns, which makes the programme substitutional rather than incremental in a +1% unit environment (A03-S9).

additional_contradictory_evidence.source: ASI Central - the supply and demand gap in women's sports merch
additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: The '1 piece of women's merchandise for every 9 men's' framing that underpins the whole supply-desert narrative dates to mid-2024. Combined with the 2026 fan assortment above, the gap is being closed by the market in real time - which is a timing risk for an SS28 delivery, and a warning that the founding statistic is two years stale and is being re-quoted as current.

Queries about 2026 WNBA merchandise performance surface Accio pages - the Alibaba AI B2B sourcing engine the auditor identified as the laundering path for A04-S5's numbers - among the top results. The public web cannot currently answer the bottoms-versus-tops question for women's basketball merchandise without recycling AI-generated SEO content. Any 'we validated this externally' claim in the Council room should be refused; only Nike's and Fanatics' own category data can settle it.

strongest_counterargument: 'We already sell this. Fanatics has a Ladies WNBA Shorts page next to the jerseys and it is full of our product - a Legends Flow Mesh short at USD 74.99, a Victory knee-length at USD 85, a Crossover WNBA at USD 60 - and we shipped a jersey-matched Rebel Fanwear short in May and a Caitlin Clark short with the logo on the leg. So tell me two things. One: what is the incremental unit, given the fixture you are asking me to secure already exists and already has three Nike shorts hanging in it? Two: why will a fourth one hold USD 65 for eight weeks, when the Logowoman is at USD 34.97 from USD 49.99, the Tri-Blend is at USD 55.99 from USD 79.99, and our own Sabrina is at USD 42.97 from USD 65? You have written a merchandising brief for a fixture that is already built, and priced it off a list wall that never realises its list.'
adjustment_rationale:
Down 20 points from 61. The demand half is untouched and I could not weaken it - three consecutive record seasons on a per-game basis, an All-Star crowd outdrawing the NBA's, 73 million unique viewers at the halfway point, a ratified seven-year CBA with the cap up roughly fivefold, growth achieved with the concentration athlete sidelined, VERIFIED Unrivaled economics (A05-S7), a VERIFIED wholesale swing (A02-S7), a first-party retailer call-out (A04-S5), and a genuinely exclusive Nike licence position on both halves of the outfit. That floor is worth roughly 40 points on its own and it is why this is not a zero.

Everything above that floor came off. The opportunity's own stated kill condition - 'if the fixture change cannot be secured, the product should not be made, because the fixture IS the opportunity' - is met in the wrong direction: the fixture is already secured, already occupied, and occupied by Nike. Fanatics runs a Ladies WNBA Shorts category stocked with Nike Legends Flow Mesh at USD 74.99, Legends Fleece at USD 74.99, On-Court Victory at USD 84.99 and Logowoman Crossover at USD 49.99; Nike's own WNBA pages carry Victory knee-length at USD 85, Basketball Fleece at USD 75 and Crossover WNBA at USD 60; Rebel Fanwear shorts have been in fan doors since 8 May 2026; the Clark collection already pairs a logo tee with a logo short. That is minus 12 on newness and differentiation, and it is the same ground on which the auditor rejected A05-O4.

Minus 6 on price: the USD 65-75 rung is argued solely from a fan-wall comparison set that is discounting 25-45% with codes, which removes the argument entirely and leaves the number contradicted on both walls in a +1% unit, ASP-mix-only environment (A03-S9, A04-S4). Minus 2 on the inference the audit told the base to discard (jersey-outfit search implying a bottom; F1 +483% and Brazil jersey +302% on the same report), and minus 2 more spread across the cross-gender buyer contradiction in the spec's own best commercial signal, the unanchored 200-230 g/m2 target, and the SKU complexity of two fabrics x two inseams x XS-3X-plus-tall x four core colours x three drop windows x per-tour-stop exclusives.

Plus 1 back, because my attack surfaced a BETTER and cheaper test than the one the spec proposes: Nike already owns the Rebel Fanwear and Caitlin Clark shorts sell-through, which measures this exact thesis in-market with no vendor, no field cost and no dependence on a private startup league's receipts.

41 means: the money should go to women's basketball, the brief should not go to the Council in this form, and the answer is very likely a block-and-proportion input routed into programmes Nike is already funding rather than a new franchise.

validation_plan.question: Is a Nike women's basketball/WNBA short ALREADY merchandised adjacent to the jersey in fan doors, and if so what is its full-price sell-through and markdown depth? This is the opportunity's own stated kill condition and my evidence says it has already been answered in the negative.
validation_plan.method: Live SKU-and-fixture audit: photograph and log the WNBA/women's basketball fan wall at 12 doors (4 Dick's, 4 Foot Locker, 2 Hibbett, 2 team/arena stores) plus screen-captures of the Fanatics Ladies WNBA Shorts, WNBAStore women's and Nike WNBA pages, recording every women's bottom by style, inseam, list price, promo price and adjacency to jerseys. Cross-check against the internal assortment file so no SKU is missed.
validation_plan.who: US Merchandising / Marketplace Ops field team, with Nike DTC digital merchandising pulling the .com and partner-site screens
validation_plan.cost_time: Roughly USD 5-8k, 1-2 weeks. Run this FIRST; if the fixture is already occupied and selling, the opportunity as written stops here.

validation_plan.question: Did the WNBA Rebel Edition Fanwear short (8 May 2026) and the Caitlin Clark short sell? At what full-price rate, what size-curve fill, what markdown, and what jersey attach rate?
validation_plan.method: Internal first-party pull - no research spend. Weekly sell-through by door and by size for Rebel Fanwear short, Clark short, WNBA Victory short, Legends Flow Mesh short and Sabrina/Crossover women's, FY26 full year rather than an August snapshot, plus basket analysis on jersey-plus-bottom co-purchase at Nike.com and, via the licensing partner, at Fanatics/WNBAStore.
validation_plan.who: Nike Basketball Apparel PLM with Global Merch Financial Planning and the WNBA licensing team; Fanatics category analytics for the partner half
validation_plan.cost_time: Near-zero cost, 2-3 weeks. This is the real decisive test and it replaces the proposed Unrivaled split, which Nike may have no right to obtain.

validation_plan.question: What share of women's basketball fan merchandise units are BOTTOMS rather than tops? Is a bottom a rounding error or a real slot? Threshold: bottoms must exceed roughly 12% of units to justify a dedicated block.
validation_plan.method: Category-mix pull by garment type (jersey / tee / hoodie / headwear / bottoms) in units and dollars from the WNBA licensing partner and Fanatics for the 2025 and 2026 seasons, plus arena-retail category splits from two or three clubs (Fever, Valkyries, Liberty) and, if obtainable under NDA, the Unrivaled Philadelphia 30 Jan 2026 USD 400,000 night split by category (A05-S7).
validation_plan.who: Nike WNBA licensing/partnership lead with Commercial Analytics; club retail directors for the arena splits
validation_plan.cost_time: USD 10-25k and 4 weeks if any external data purchase is needed; potentially near-zero via existing licensing relationships.

validation_plan.question: Does a USD 65-75 women's fan bottom hold at full price for eight consecutive weeks in a fan fixture, or must it be costed to USD 50-55?
validation_plan.method: Do not run a new price test first. Instead pull list-versus-realised ASP and markdown rate by week for every women's basketball and WNBA fanwear bottom across FY25-FY26 by door - the audit's explicit precondition for treating any price in this portfolio as a recommendation. Only if that shows a durable full-price band above USD 60 should a live eight-week full-price holdback be run on the existing Legends Flow Mesh and Victory knee-length shorts in matched fan doors.
validation_plan.who: Nike Global Merch Financial Planning and Pricing, with the Dick's/Foot Locker account team
validation_plan.cost_time: Data pull near-zero, 2-3 weeks. Live holdback, if warranted, USD 15-30k over 8-10 weeks.

validation_plan.question: Does a women's high-rise, untapered block actually beat the current women's grade on the OUTFIT occasion - and does the volume buyer even want a women's-specific block, given Ed Stack described 'boys and girls, young men and women' buying this product?
validation_plan.method: Wear-and-styling test, n>=200 women aged 16-35 who own a women's basketball jersey, in three US markets, evaluating rise, leg-line, hem width and hang with a jersey TUCKED - benchmarked against ISoFly 6.5/7in, Crossover 5in, Sabrina, and the in-market fan shorts (Legends Flow Mesh, Rebel Fanwear) as controls rather than against a blank. Add a parallel cell of n>=100 male fan buyers to test whether a unisex fan block in a women's size run outperforms a women's-specific block. Mine the existing 105-athlete WNBA council focus groups for rise and waistband preference before fielding anything new.
validation_plan.who: Nike Consumer Insights with Apparel Design and Advanced Product Creation; WNBA player council access via Sports Marketing
validation_plan.cost_time: USD 40-60k, 6-8 weeks. Gate this behind items 1-3; do not fund block development or tooling before they clear.

validation_plan.question: Do the basketball terms in the Pinterest Summer 2026 data carry any meaningful ABSOLUTE volume, or is a +494% sitting on a base too small to be a market alongside F1 at +483% and Brazil jersey at +302%?
validation_plan.method: Request the underlying term list ranked by absolute search-and-save volume through Nike's Pinterest partnership, and compare basketball terms against motorsport and football terms on the same base. Triangulate with actual women's non-jersey sportswear sell-through in the US and Australia (A02-S9) before any of it is treated as a basketball demand signal, per the audit's explicit instruction.
validation_plan.who: Nike Global Brand Marketing / Media Partnerships with Consumer Insights
validation_plan.cost_time: USD 0-10k, 3 weeks. If basketball is a small base growing fast alongside larger pan-sport bases, the aesthetic belongs to Sportswear or Football, not Basketball.
